 Order

1 .  The petitioner herein in the instant petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has prayed for the following reliefs:-
i.

By issuance of a writ of certiorari or any other writ, order or direction, quashing the impugned consideration order bearing No. 09 of 2015 dated 12.10.2015 by respondent No.3;
ii.

By issuance of a writ of mandamus or any other writ, order or direction, the respondents be directed to assess and pay compensation to petitioner for acquisition of land (annexure-I), situated at Aklipora, Razwan, Tehsil Beerwa District Budgam, in which power transmission towers/polls have been erected as also with respect to the land (shown in Annexure-I), over which overhead power transmission lines have been laid by respondent department;
iii.

By issuance of a writ of mandamus or any other writ, order or direction, the respondents be directed to pay compensation to petitioner with respect to fruit bearing and non-fruit bearing trees,
plants, shrubs etc, existing in the land properties of petitioner, situated at Aklipora, Razwan, Tehsil Beerwa District Budgam, over which power transmission towers/polls have been erected as also overhead power transmission lines have been laid by respondent department.

sentences.text:
The facts giving rise to the filing of the instant petition as stated in the petition are that the 5 marlas out of one kanal of property of land of the petitioner comprising under survey No. 372 situated at Akilpora, Razwan, Tehsil Beerwa District Budgam came under a process of acquisition and laying of power transmission lines for construction of transmission towers as a consequence whereof, compensation on a lower side came to be paid by the respondents to the petitioner as against the other similarly situated land holders which compelled the petitioner to approach the respondents and also file an application before Deputy Commissioner, Budgam, making a request therein for shifting of the transmission towers and returning back of the land acquired from the petitioner to the petitioner, which application came to be forwarded by the Deputy Commissioner,
Budgam to the Executive Engineer, Transmission Line, Construction Division, 1st Bemina, Srinagar who in response thereto furnished a report that the request of shifting of the tower cannot be considered owing to the technical feasibility as the transmission route stood already approved through Central Electricity Authority, Government of India and that the strip of land in question stands notified under section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, along with the land of other land holders and that on account of failure of the respondents to redress the grievance of the petitioner projected before them and compelled the petitioner to approach this Court and file OWP No.
1472/2015 which petition came to be disposed of on 21.08.2015 with a direction to the respondents to accord consideration to the petitioner's claim as set out in the petition, in the light of the averments made in the petition, annexures appended thereto and the rules occupying the field and that the respondents despite the service of the said order upon them failed to implement the same necessitating the filing of a contempt petition before this Court being CPOWP No. 316/2016, in response to which contempt petition, the contemnors filed statement of facts, stating therein that the claim of the petitioner came to be thoroughly examined and considered on the touch stone of rules and was found to be untenable and consequently rejected in terms of order dated 12.10.2015,
whereupon the said contempt petition came to be settled by this Court providing a liberty to the petitioner to work out a remedy against the said rejection order 12.10.2015, whereupon the petitioner filed the instant petition.
3.

The petitioner has challenged the order dated 12.10.2015 on multiple grounds in the instant petition including on the ground that the same is unlawful, unconstitutional having been issued arbitrarily against the settled principles of law.

4. Objections to the petition have been filed by the respondents wherein it is being admitted that the petitioner is amongst the land owners whose land came to be acquired for construction of transmission towers/transmission lines and upon an assessment received, 5 marlas of land belonging to the petitioner came to be acquired and compensation thereof came to be assessed and determined in private negotiations in the year 2008 and consequently compensation thereof paid to the petitioner and, such, petitioner cannot claim any further compensation thereof once accepted by him.

It is further stated in the objections that the compensation of trees which came under the corridor of the transmission line and were necessarily to be cut came also to be assessed by the competent authority and compensation thereof paid accordingly, stating further in the objections that no further compensation is allowed to the land of the petitioner which came under the corridor of Ghulam Mohi Uddin Sheikh vs Union Territory Of J And K And Ors on 6 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28961594/
2 transmission line and that the claim raised by the petitioner for compensation of land coming under the transmission line is not permissible in view of law settled by a Division Bench of this Court in case titled as "Ranvijay Chand and Anr. Vs State of J&K and Ors. passed in LPA (W)No. 131/2001".
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5.

entities.text: Ranvijay Chand and Anr. Vs State of J&K and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The short grievance projected by the petitioner in the instant petition is two fold, firstly, that the compensation paid to him qua the land acquired by the respondents is inadequate and secondly,
that the respondents did not pay any compensation to the petitioner qua the land through which the transmission line and passes through.

Insofar the first grievance of the petitioner qua inadequacy of the compensation is concerned, record tends to show that the petitioner has received compensation qua the acquired land after the same came to be assessed and determined in private negotiations in presence of the petitioner, as such,
the petitioner in law is estopped from joining any issue in this regard.

Insofar as the second grievance projected by the petitioner that the respondents did not pay compensation to the petitioner for the land through which the transmission line is passing through as the said land allegedly has become incapable of being used by the petitioner, is concerned, the law admittedly in this regard stands settled by a Division Bench of this Court in the aforesaid judgment titled as "Ranvijay Chand and Anr. Vs State of J&K and Ors. reported in 2005 (1) JKJ (236)"
wherein it has been,inter alia, held that a land holder cannot assert any right, legal, fundamental or constitutional right qua transmission line the aerial right of way in respect of transmission lines continues to be with the state and individual owners cannot claim compensation in respect thereof.
In presence ofthe aforesaid position of law laid down by the Division Bench in the judgment supra,
this Court has no reason to take a different view in the instant matter for the aforesaid issue raised by the petitioner.
6.

sentences.text: Viewed thus, in the aforesaid backdrop there is no merit in the petition and same accordingly isdismissed.

(JAVED IQBAL WANI) JUDGE SRINAGAR 06.06.2024 "S.Nuzhat"
